record.paper_title: Padua points and “fake” nodes for polynomial approximation: old, new and open problems
record.original_question: For Morrow-Patterson points in the square [-1,1]^2, which form a unisolvent total-degree interpolation set of N=(n+2 choose 2) points equidistributed with respect to the square's Dubiner metric, can one prove the numerically observed Lebesgue-constant bound Λ_MP=O(n^2) as the degree n grows?

evidence.quote: Numerically, we actually found a growth of O(n^2). So this is an open problem to show that the ΛMP = O(n^2).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n\ge 1$ be an integer and set $N=\binom{n+2}{2}$. The Morrow–Patterson points in the square $[-1,1]^2$ are the $N$-point total-degree unisolvent interpolation set defined (up to standard normalization) by
$$\big(x_i,y_j\big)=\Big(\cos\tfrac{i\pi}{n+2},\ \cos\tfrac{j\pi}{n+2}\Big),$$
with $(i,j)$ ranging over an interlacing pattern of integer pairs such that exactly $N$ nodes are selected and total-degree polynomial interpolation of degree $n$ is unisolvent. These nodes are known to be equidistributed with respect to the Dubiner metric on the square. For a unisolvent set $X=\{P_1,\dots,P_N\}\subset[-1,1]^2$ for the space $\mathbb{P}_n^2$ of bivariate polynomials of total degree at most $n$, with associated Lagrange basis $\{\ell_k\}_{k=1}^N$, the Lebesgue constant is
$$\Lambda(X)=\max_{(x,y)\in[-1,1]^2}\sum_{k=1}^{N}|\ell_k(x,y)|.$$
Let $\Lambda_{MP}(n)$ denote the Lebesgue constant of the Morrow–Patterson points of parameter $n$. Prove that
$$\Lambda_{MP}(n)=O(n^2)\quad\text{as }n\to\infty,$$
i.e., there exists a constant $C>0$ independent of $n$ such that $\Lambda_{MP}(n)\le C n^2$ for all sufficiently large $n$.
artifact.status_search_result: A 2024 preprint by Bos, Caliari, De Marchi and Vianello titled "On the Lebesgue constant of the Morrow–Patterson points" (arXiv:2412.14595), published in Constructive Approximation (2025), proves the conjectured O(n^2) growth, confirming the numerical observation from Caliari et al. (2005) and improving prior upper bounds of order n^6 (Bos) and n^3 (via hyperinterpolation).

status_evidence.title: On the Lebesgue constant of the Morrow-Patterson points
status_evidence.snippet: We prove that the Lebesgue constant of the Morrow-Patterson points grows like O(n^2), confirming a 20-year-old conjecture based on numerical evidence.
status_evidence.claim: The O(n^2) upper bound for the Lebesgue constant of the Morrow-Patterson points has been proved.

status_evidence.title: On the Lebesgue Constant of the Morrow–Patterson Points
status_evidence.snippet: Published in Constructive Approximation, 2025; establishes Λ_MP = O(n^2).
status_evidence.claim: Journal publication confirming the resolution of the open problem.
